text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The French comic dramatist MOLIERE ("Le Misanthrope") was born as JEAN BAPTISTE POQUELIN on this day in 1622. He was often dubbed the "Father of French comedy".
English journalist JOHN CLARK was born in 1830, and played a significant part in founding the South Australian Royal
Society and the State Library.
Beatified Australian teacher and nun MOTHER MARY McKILLOP was born on this day in 1842. She was the founder of the SISTERS OF ST JOSEPH OF THE SACRED HEART.
ARISTOTLE ONASSIS, the Greek shipowner and second husband of JACKIE KENNEDY, was born in 1906.
American actor LLOYD BRIDGES was born on this day in 1913.
American civil-rights leader, clergyman and winner of the 1964 NOBEL PEACE PRIZE, MARTIN LUTHER KING, was born in 1929.
Child actress MARGARET O'BRIEN, who won a special ACADEMY AWARD in 1944 at the age of 7, was born in 1937.

American lead singer and songwriter for 'Lynyrd Skynyrd' RONALD WAYNE VAN ZANDT was born in 1948. The group's first hit was "Sweet Home Alabama". This was also their biggest hit. Just as the group was about to became one of the most successful southern rock bands three members, including VAN ZANDT, were killed in a plane crash.
** EVENTS **
1535 : In England, HENRY VIII became Supreme Head of the
Church under the Act of Supremacy.
1559 : Queen ELIZABETH I was crowned Queen of England at
the age of 26, succeeding to the throne from her half-sister MARY TUDOR.
1790 : FLETCHER CHRISTIAN and the other mutineers from
the "BOUNTY" landed on PITCAIRN ISLAND in the South Pacific.
1878 : Women received degrees for the first time at
LONDON UNIVERSITY.
1880 : The first telephone directory was published in
London.
1914 : English boys aged 15 to 19 were offered assisted
passages to work on South Australian farms. The boys were paid pocket money and the South Australian State Treasury held the balance of their pay until they turned 21.
1919 : Communist leader ROSA LUXEMBOURG was murdered
along with KARL LEIBKNECHT after the failure of their uprising in Berlin.
1931 : Melbourne police commissioner THOMAS BLAMEY warned
pedestrians to obey traffic lights, following complaints from motorists that people were ignoring the new devices.
1946 : Melbourne authorities revealed that the platypus
sent to British Prime Minister WINSTON CHURCHILL had died four days after it arrived in Britain.
1953 : Greek shipping magnate ARISTOTLE ONASSIS gained
control of the Monte Carlo Casino. He added the casino to his 91 ships and offices and homes in six countries.
1962 : Fashion designer YVES ST LAURENT opened his own
couture house in Prais. He was the protege of CHRISTIAN DIOR and took over his salon at the age of 21, when DIOR died. He has said his aim is to make women look elegant and well-groomed.
1970 : Australian Prime Minister JOHN GORTON called for a
halt to all oil drilling off the Queensland coast, pending an inquiry into the possible dangers to the Great Barrier Reef.
1971 : The currency of Britain changed from pounds,
shillings and pence, to the decimal pound of 100 new pence.
1973 : US President RICHARD NIXON announced an end to all
bombing of Vietnam by American warplanes.
1990 : Thousands of East Germans attacked the
headquarters of the STASI (the old regime's Secret Police) in Berlin.
1996 : Greek Socialist Prime Minister ANDREAS PAPANDREOU
resigned for health reasons.
